Mirroring undoes each flip: in this mirror image a **flipped** letter reads normally, and an unflipped one reads backwards.

ceed-2024-q28:
In animation, **more frames go where the object moves slowly or changes a lot**. This is the **slow-in, slow-out** rule (also called ease in and ease out): drawings bunch up close together where motion slows, and spread far apart where it is fast.

- **C (the peak):** the fish loses its upward speed, hangs for a moment and turns from nose-up to nose-down. Each frame moves it only slightly, so this point needs the most drawings. **Answer: C.**
- **A:** the fish bursts out of the water at top speed, so it needs few, widely spaced frames.
- **B:** it is still rising quickly, partway up, so the frames are spaced fairly wide.
- **D:** gravity has sped it back up as it dives, so again it needs few frames.
